applies_why: The judge is weighing a chain-against-chain collision (the challenger's seed/loins chain versus the defender's chain), which is exactly the situation K-C governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side
room: The judge's 'does not name Joseph as the begetter' (and 'rests on the woman-route inference') read either as footing observations (each chain's footing stops short of, or runs only through inference to, the contested link -- a clean footing weigh) or as the retired stating-verse test (faulting an already-footed chain for lacking any verse that states the claim in its own words); I weighed the second reading, because footing was granted to both chains before the faults were assigned, leaving only absence of explicit statement as the operative ground.
why: After finding both chains footed, the judge drove the UNDERDETERMINED verdict by discounting each chain for lacking explicit statement -- the challenger's for not naming Joseph as begetter, the defender's for resting on inference -- which is the stating-verse test K-C retires at a judge's seat for either side, not weighing by footing.
